A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Nova study and contain the complete main text and Appendix A.1–A.9. Tables, equations, and figures support reliable comparison; figure text missing from v7's extraction remains visible in its rendered pages.

before.justification: v6 reports original Nova experiments on binary decompilation and binary code similarity detection, alongside ablations, embedding analyses, and case studies in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v7 retains these original experimental results, including HumanEval-Decompile performance, binary similarity results, and the appendix's ablations and analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same hierarchical attention components, functionality and optimization contrastive objectives, embedding construction, and downstream fine-tuning procedures. Applying hierarchical attention to half the attention heads is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use AnghaBench and The-Stack for pre-training, HumanEval-Decompile for decompilation evaluation, and BinaryCorp-3M plus the same six evaluation projects for binary similarity. No task, architecture domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same decompilation and long-input comparators. Tables 6–9 retain jTrans, DiEmph, and CodeArt, and the appendix retains the same ablation and case-study comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.2 preserve the training settings, preprocessing, model sizes, and evaluation procedures. Both specify 20 decompilation samples at temperature 0.2 and top-p 0.95, and binary similarity candidate pools of 50, 100, 200, and 500.

E4.justification: The component ablations, half-versus-all attention-head comparison, decompilation case studies, t-SNE/PCA analyses, and attention visualizations are retained. Appendix material moves with page reflow, but no analysis or tested question changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The decompilation sampling procedure and point-estimate reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 2–15 and the plotted and case-study findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains Nova-1.3B's average Pass@1/Pass@10 of 25.17/38.30 and Nova-6.7B's 34.36/46.91.

T1.justification: The embedding definitions, functionality constraint, contrastive losses, combined objective, and downstream objectives in Section 3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims for hierarchical attention and contrastive learning. Their claimed novelty, scope, and downstream benefits are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations, embedding separation, and attention patterns are retained. Appendix A.9 preserves the same X86-specific training and model-scale limitations, while proposed extensions remain future work.

D1.justification: v7 newly discloses use of Purdue's Anvil through ACCESS allocation CIS240304 in the acknowledgments. This adds computing-resource provenance; Appendix A.2's hardware, software, hyperparameters, and the model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v7 adds Boerner et al. (2023), the ACCESS infrastructure reference, to support the new acknowledgment. Section 2 and the paper's positioning relative to earlier scientific methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments gain a short computing-support statement, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several figures, including the code examples and embedding plots, become raster images while retaining their content. The expanded acknowledgments and bibliography cause limited reference and appendix reflow; table structures and figure numbering remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v7 adds useful Anvil/ACCESS attribution and its reference, but retains the same methods, evidence, technical instructions, interpretations, and limitations. Figure rasterization and page reflow introduce modest presentation differences without a meaningful overall gain or loss in paper quality.
